commodity_commentary: Canadian-relevant commodities diverged sharply across categories in the week ending March 30, 2026 — energy prices advanced across the board, with WTI crude crossing US$100/bbl for the first time since July 2022 on the continued Strait of Hormuz disruption, while precious metals retreated, with gold down 14% month-over-month despite elevated geopolitical tensions, driven by margin liquidation and a stronger US dollar1,4. The WCS-WTI discount narrowed to an estimated US$15.74/bbl, holding at a historical spread for Canadian heavy crude producers3. Base metals were mixed, with copper elevated at US$5.76/lb and nickel under pressure, while uranium declined on risk-off sentiment7. The database tracks 42 oil and gas projects ($93.8 billion) and 317 power energy projects ($487 billion) linked to commodity price levels across Canada2.

commodities.name: WTI Crude Oil
commodities.commentary: WTI Crude Oil: US$102.88/bbl (+5.5% week-over-week) — the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz since approximately March 2, disrupting an estimated 20 million barrels per day (~20% of global seaborne oil flows), drove WTI to its first settlement above US$100 since July 2022; tanker traffic through the strait dropped approximately 70%1. The Dallas Fed estimated that a one-quarter closure could raise WTI to a US$98/bbl average and reduce global GDP growth by an annualized 2.9 percentage points in Q2 20265. The database tracks 42 oil and gas projects ($93.8 billion) across Canada, concentrated in Alberta oil sands and offshore Newfoundland and Labrador2. WTI is up approximately 50% month-over-month1.

commodities.name: Western Canadian Select
commodities.commentary: Western Canadian Select: US$87.14/bbl — the WCS-WTI differential is estimated at US$15.74/bbl, reflecting the ongoing cost disadvantage for Canadian heavy crude producers relative to the West Texas benchmark3. The database tracks 42 oil and gas projects ($93.8 billion) across Alberta and Saskatchewan in which producer netback prices reference WCS-linked pricing2. Pipeline capacity through the expanded Trans Mountain system partially constrains the differential from widening further3.

commodities.name: Brent Crude
commodities.commentary: Brent Crude: US$112.57/bbl — Brent surged approximately 55% in March, a record monthly gain for the contract since its inception in 1988, as the Strait of Hormuz disruption rippled through global oil markets1. Brent peaked at approximately US$126/bbl intra-month before retreating on reports of potential US-Iran diplomatic talks1. The Brent-WTI spread of approximately US$9.69/bbl reflects elevated Atlantic Basin demand and longer tanker routing via the Cape of Good Hope.

commodities.name: Natural Gas (Henry Hub)
commodities.commentary: Natural Gas (Henry Hub): US$2.94/MMBtu — Henry Hub and the Canadian AECO benchmark rose as global LNG demand spiked in response to Middle East supply disruptions6. The EIA's March 10 short-term energy outlook projected Henry Hub averaging US$3.80/MMBtu for full-year 20266. The database tracks 317 power and energy projects ($487 billion), including BC LNG infrastructure and Alberta natural gas processing facilities, affected by shifting gas price levels2.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.commentary: Gold: US$4,578/oz — gold declined more than 14% in March, on pace for its steepest monthly decline since October 2008, as margin liquidation and US dollar strength drove sellers despite elevated geopolitical tensions4. Gold peaked at approximately US$5,161/oz on March 3 before retreating. The database tracks mining projects across BC, Ontario, and Quebec that reference gold price levels in feasibility parameters2.

commodities.name: Silver
commodities.commentary: Silver: US$73.33/oz — silver tracked the broader precious metals retreat in March alongside gold's margin-driven decline4. Ontario and BC silver mining operations factor into the database's tracked mining project inventory2.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.commentary: Copper: US$5.76/lb — copper held in an elevated range of US$5.25–$6.01/lb in March, reflecting mixed signals from China's manufacturing PMI recovery to 50.4 in March and global supply chain disruption from Middle East instability7,8. BC and Ontario copper mining projects tracked in the database reference price levels above the current spot for long-run feasibility thresholds2. Electrification-driven demand across grid and EV supply chain investment in Canada continues to support copper's demand profile7.

commodities.name: Aluminum
commodities.commentary: Aluminum: US$3,423/MT — aluminum prices reflect elevated energy input costs following the Strait of Hormuz supply disruption, given the metal's energy-intensive smelting process1. Canadian aluminum production, concentrated in Quebec smelting operations, contributes to export volumes subject to ongoing US tariff measures9.

commodities.name: Lumber
commodities.commentary: Lumber: US$610/MBF — live lumber price data has been unavailable from the primary timeseries data source since May 2023 due to a ticker or data feed issue; the US$610/MBF figure is sourced from the task brief10. BC forestry operations and residential construction projects in the database — including 211 residential projects tracked nationally — use lumber as a primary input cost benchmark2.

commodities.name: Uranium
commodities.commentary: Uranium: US$92/lb — uranium declined approximately 17% month-over-month alongside broader risk-off sentiment in metals; the URA ETF proxy fell to US$46.86 and Cameco (CCO.TO) closed at C$147.75, down approximately 14% month-over-month4. Saskatchewan is home to the majority of Canada's uranium production, including Cameco operations at Cigar Lake and McArthur River2.

commodities.name: Nickel
commodities.commentary: Nickel: US$14,641/MT (US$6.64/lb) — nickel moved under pressure in March as battery supply chain demand signals from China's manufacturing sector remained mixed despite the PMI returning above 508. Ontario (Vale, Glencore), Manitoba, and Labrador nickel mining operations link to the database's tracked mineral project inventory2.

commodities.name: Canola
commodities.commentary: Canola: C$733/MT — Prairie canola pricing reflects export demand conditions with China as a primary destination, subject to ongoing bilateral trade dynamics9. Saskatchewan and Alberta crushing capacity and oilseed storage infrastructure projects tracked in the database reference canola throughput volumes2.

commodities.name: Potash
commodities.commentary: Potash: US$355/MT — Nutrien (NTR.TO) traded at approximately C$104.62, down 1.0% week-over-week and up 1.0% month-over-month, indicating broadly stable potash benchmark pricing4. Saskatchewan potash operations, including Nutrien and Mosaic production sites, account for approximately 30% of global potash supply and link to several extraction projects in the database2.

commodities.name: Iron Ore
commodities.commentary: Iron Ore: price data not obtained in the current data refresh period — no current figure available from the tracked timeseries2. Iron ore pricing affects Quebec and Labrador iron ore pellet operations, including those linked to the Labrador Trough mining corridor tracked in the project database2.

wcs_analysis.analysis_text: The Western Canadian Select differential to WTI was approximately US$15.74/bbl in the week ending March 30, 2026. At the current WCS netback, Canadian heavy crude producers receive US$87.14/bbl before transportation and processing costs. The database tracks 42 oil and gas projects ($93.8 billion) for which WCS-linked producer pricing is a key economic input. Pipeline capacity through the expanded Trans Mountain system provides an export corridor to tidewater that partially constrains discount widening relative to historical pre-TMX levels.
